refnamediv.refpurpose: View ringbuffer statistics in a system

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: This program periodically polls the ring monitor and displays statistics for all ringbuffers in the system. If the optional host is provided the statistics for the ringbuffers in host are displayed. If omitted, the statistics for the ringbuffers in localhost are displayed. Note that proxy rings are also displayed.
For this to work properly, the ring_monitor server must be running in the host being viewed. See the man page entry for ring_monitor. Normally this should be started at system startup.
The statistics are displayed in a simple table with the following columns:

listitem.para: The name of the ring buffer whose statistics are displayed on this line.
The total number of bytes that have passed through the ring since the ring_monitor started (see BUGS below).
Same as Total Volume however this statistic is cleared when a BEGIN_RUN is observed in the ring.
Total number of PHYSICS_EVENT items observed in the ring since the ring_monitor was statrted.
Total number of PHYSICS_EVENT items but reset when a BEGIN_RUN item is observed in the ring.
Instantaneous bytes per second throughput through the ringbuffer.
Instantaneous rate of PHYSICS_EVENT items observed in the ringbuffer.

refsect1.para: You can sort the table by any of the columns by clicking on that column's header. You can stretch each column's width as well. The initial sort is by ring buffer name, though you may find it useful to sort by rate.
Note that since there is only one ring_monitor server running in the target system, the impact of the statsview program on the system and throughput is negligible.

refsect1.title: BUGS
refsect1.para: WHen a ringbuffer is deleted, the ring master, in the system the ringbuffer lived in will kill all clients (producer and consumers) that are attached to that ring. This means that the ring_monitor will be killed as well. The ring_monitor, however consists of a parent process that spawns off the actual monitor and, when the actual monitor exits restarts it. Unfortunately that means that all counters maintained by the ring_monitor are reset when a ringbuffer is deleted. This is not expected to be fixed.

Since all of the statsview statistics come from the ring_monitor, the totals columns will be reset for all remaining rings. The statsview program will, however remove deleted rings from the table and will tolarate being unable to update statistics during the time the ring_monitor restarts.

refnamediv.refpurpose: Plot time evolution of ring statistics

refsect1.title: DESCRIPTION
refsect1.para: The ring monitor program can told to write a periodic log of ring buffer statistics. The statsplot program can then produce plots of that data over any time range covered by the data in that file.

When started, the program opens the statistics-file read-only and produces a tabbed notebook with a tab page for each ring buffer seen in the statistics file. The intial view covers all data since the beginning of the current day.

Each page of the notebook has a control panel. The control panel features a radio button set which allows the user to select data either from a start date/time, before an end date/time, or between a start and end date/time.

The date/times for the query are selected via date/time editors above the radio buttons. Only the relevant date/time editors are enabled, depending on the state of the radio button set. Dates can be selected from a calendar by clicking the down arrow to the right of the editor. The date and time fields can also be selected by clicking on it and typing new values for each Month/Day/Year field. The up and down arrow keys can also be used to increment date and time fields by one.
Once you have selected a date/time range, click the Update to plot the data in the seleted tab. Note that the date/time periods of each page in the notebook are independent.

Each page provides 6 plots, from top left to right:
The number of events seen since the most recent BEGIN_RUN ring item in the ring.
The instantaneous data rate in bytes/sec through the ring.
The event rate through the in events/sec through the ring. An event is defined as a ring item of type PHYSICS_EVENT
The total data volume (bytes) through the ring.
The total data volume (bytes) through the ring since the last BEGIN_RUN item was seen.
The total number of events through the ring since the last BEGIN_RUN item. An event is defineds as a PHYSICS_EVENT ring item.

Notes:
If there is no data within the selected time range, a dialog box indicating that will pop up and the plots displayed will not be modified. If there is no data in the database since the beginning of the day in which the program is run, the initial plots will not be drawn.
If the data in the file do not extend to the end date/time, the time axis on the plot will terminate at the date/time the data actually terminates.
You can point the program at the file that the ring monitor program is accumulating into and, by setting the end date beyond the current date/time, watch the live statistics evolve by clicking the update button to observe new statistics accumulated by the ring monitor.
While the ring monitor timestamps data as times relative to the unix epoch, the plots display the times in the local timezone for your convenience.
